does: Rolls cold, firm croqueta paste into small logs or balls and coats each one in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs in turn, so that it fries with a crisp shell and a soft, creamy middle.

intro.what: Croquetas are formed from cold firm paste and coated in flour, egg and crumbs.
intro.why: It teaches you to handle a creamy centre while building a complete shell around it.

how: Set out shallow dishes in a row: flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs, in that order. Have a tray ready.
Scoop a spoonful of the chilled paste and roll it between floured hands into a short log or a ball. Keep them all one size.
Roll each one in the flour and shake off the extra, turn it through the egg, then roll it in the crumbs, pressing so that they cover it all round.
Lay them on the tray without touching. For a thicker shell, dip them in the egg and the crumbs a second time.
Chill them again for a short while before frying, so that the shell sets.

cues.text: The paste rolls clean between floured hands and does not stick.
Each croqueta is covered all round with an even coat of crumbs and no bare patch.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving a bare patch, through which the paste bursts out in the hot oil.
mistakes.fix: Turn each one through the egg and the crumbs until it is covered all round.

mistakes.mistake: Shaping warm paste, which squashes and sticks to the hands.
mistakes.fix: Chill the paste until it is firm, and flour your hands.

mistakes.mistake: Using the same hand for the dry coats and for the egg, which builds up gluey lumps on the fingers.
mistakes.fix: Keep one hand for the flour and the crumbs and the other for the egg.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of the crumb shell?
choices: A loose dusting that falls away in the oil.
A replacement for firming the paste.
A crisp outside around a soft creamy middle.
quiz.because: The coating encloses the shaped paste and creates a contrasting crisp exterior.

quiz.question: How can gluey lumps on the fingers be reduced?
choices: Keep a hand for dry coatings and the other for egg.
Use egg-coated fingers in the crumb bowl each time.
Mix flour, egg and crumbs into a paste first.
quiz.because: Separating wet and dry handling limits coating building up on the fingers.

quiz.question: Which appearance matters before frying?
choices: Loose crumbs around an exposed paste centre.
An even crumb coat without bare patches.
A heavy coating only on the ends.
quiz.because: Bare areas interrupt the shell and give soft filling a route out.

quiz.question: The paste squashes and sticks during shaping. What should change?
choices: Shape it warmer with more pressure.
Add the egg coating before forming a shape.
Chill it until firm and flour the hands.
quiz.because: Cold firm paste is easier to handle without collapsing into the hands.

comes_after.why: There is nothing to shape until the paste has been made and chilled.

variant_of.differs: The food is a soft paste that has to be rolled to shape first, and it takes flour, then egg, then crumbs, so that the shell holds the paste in when it is fried. The coat of a cutlet goes straight onto firm meat with egg or mustard and crumbs.
